title: HTTP handlers (do_GET/do_POST/do_PUT/do_DELETE) are never exercised by tests
evidence: test_app.py tests only normalize() (app.py:45), book_id() (app.py:129) and raw SQLite CRUD via connect() (app.py:12); no test issues an HTTP request, so status codes (201/200/404/400/204), JSON serialization, and ?author= query parsing in do_GET (app.py:60-83) are untested. test_coverage=0.48 (scores.json). Agent log notes the sandbox blocked socket binding, so it dropped the in-process HTTP tests it originally wrote.
suggestion: Drive the handler in-process (e.g. instantiate BooksHandler against a BytesIO rfile/wfile, or use http.client against a threaded server on port 0) so the routing + status-code + JSON paths are covered.

title: DELETE returns 204 with a 'null' JSON body
evidence: app.py:127 do_DELETE calls send_json(204, None); send_json (app.py:27) json.dumps(None) -> 'null' and sets Content-Length: 4, so the 204 No Content response carries a 4-byte body (RFC 7231 §6.3.5: 204 must not include a body).
suggestion: For 204 send an empty body with no Content-Length (or return 200 with the deleted resource).

title: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs on every request
evidence: app.py:12-22 connect() issues the DDL each call, and every handler opens a fresh connection per request (app.py:67,76,94,109,122); schema setup and connection creation repeat on every HTTP call.
suggestion: Create the schema once at startup and reuse or pool a connection; acceptable for a demo but adds per-request overhead.
